meta: A harp-playing muse in an arched niche, engraved by Marcantonio Raimondi in 1511 from a design by Raphael.
about: A woman stands in an arched niche with a harp held against her body. She is one of the muses, and the print belongs to a series of sixteen that also show Apollo, Minerva and other women. Marcantonio Raimondi engraved them after designs by Raphael. Fine parallel lines model the folds of her gown and the shadow inside the niche. The niche frames her. The Rijksmuseum dates the sheet to 1511.

meta: Strength and Peace as two female figures in an oval, etched by Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo in 1753 after a lost fresco design.
about: Two female figures stand for Strength, who has a column, and Peace, who holds an olive branch and looks down from the clouds. Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo etched the allegory in 1753. It follows a modello by Giovanni Battista Tiepolo for a fresco in the Pietà church in Venice. The fresco itself is lost. A small cherub flies above the seated figure, and a second child rests near a stone pedestal.

meta: The Holy Family leaving a city gate on the flight into Egypt, one of 27 etchings by Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo.
about: A donkey is led through a vaulted stone gateway, with a figure in a light robe beside it and a man carrying a staff. Onlookers in headscarves and turbans gather at the right. This is the Holy Family leaving a city on the flight into Egypt. Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo etched a series of twenty-seven prints on the subject, and this is one of them. The impression lacks the number 7 beside the signature at the lower centre, a state that Rizzi described in 1971.

meta: Broken Roman arches and a distant city in a misty landscape print by Hercules Segers, held on loan by the Rijksmuseum.
about: Broken arches and walls fill the foreground of this misty print by Hercules Segers, and a city lies across a flat plain toward distant hills. The sheet belongs to the City of Amsterdam. The collector Michiel Hinloopen of Amsterdam owned it and bequeathed it to the city in 1708. It has been on loan to the Rijksmuseum since 1885.

meta: Hercules Segers's large etching of the ruined abbey of Rijnsburg, printed in yellowish white on black-ground paper.
about: Crumbling brick walls overgrown with trees and ivy rise over a man and some sheep in Hercules Segers's large view of the ruined abbey of Rijnsburg. Segers used crosshatching for tone and printed the etching in yellowish white on paper prepared with a black ground. The sheet was then coloured with opaque blue and red paint. Pieter Cornelis, Baron van Leyden, once owned it. His daughter sold his collection in 1807 to Louis Napoléon Bonaparte, King of Holland, for the Koninklijke Bibliotheek. The museum received the sheet from that library in 1816.

meta: The hunt, a 1541 woodcut by Cornelis Anthonisz. from a series of six, with Sorgheloos, Weelde and Gemack in a landscape.
about: Sorgheloos and Weelde ride through a landscape while Gemack walks beside them with a large lance, a sword and two hunting dogs. The woodcut is one of a series of six. Cornelis Anthonisz. made it in 1541. A walled town and a river lie in the distance. This impression comes without the frame and text that belong with it.

meta: Two tall trees over a grassy field, a pen and brown ink drawing by Gerbrand van den Eeckhout, given to the Rijksmuseum in 1898.
about: Two tall trees rise from a grassy field in this pen and brown ink drawing by Gerbrand van den Eeckhout, with a low fence and a dirt path leading toward distant hills. The sheet was sold at auction in Amsterdam in 1873 for 21 guilders and went to the dealer Engelberts, who bought it for Leonard Marius Beels van Heemstede. His widow, Agnes Henriette Beels van Heemstede-van Loon, gave it to the museum in 1898 together with many other drawings.

meta: A young man reclining with a book, drawn in brush and brown ink by Gerbrand van den Eeckhout, bought by the Rijksmuseum in 1948.
about: A young man in a wide-brimmed hat and lace collar lies on his stomach with his chin on one hand and an open book in front of him. Gerbrand van den Eeckhout drew him with the point of a brush and brown ink, adding brown wash. The sheet sold at auction in Amsterdam in 1910 for 1,025 guilders to the dealer Artaria of Vienna. It is later recorded in the collection of Prince Franz Josef II of Liechtenstein. The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1948 through the dealer Walter Feilchenfeldt of Zurich.

meta: A tea party in James McNeill Whistler's garden at Cheyne Walk, Chelsea, in June 1891, with named guests around the table.
about: Tea is served in the garden of James Abbott McNeill Whistler's house at Cheyne Walk in Chelsea. The visit took place in June 1891. Around the table sit Walter Sickert, Sidney Starr and Brandon Thomas with his wife, and next to them Beatrix Whistler and Ethel Birnie Philip. A standing attendant waits near the teapot and cups. Leafy trees close the scene overhead.

meta: Five trout on a pale blue ground with a poem about the Tama river, a second edition print by Utagawa Hiroshige.
about: Five trout swim against a pale blue ground, with a poem about the trout of the Tama river written beside them. The Rijksmuseum's impression is a second edition, with the publisher's stamp of Eijodo, also called Nishimuraya Yohachi. Catalogues of the first edition describe brown fish with the wood grain of the blue block showing through. Later printings are looser. In some, the lower character of the signature is broken.

meta: Christ and the woman accused of adultery, etched by Jacopo Palma the Younger for a drawing book published by Giacomo Franco in 1611.
about: Christ faces the woman accused of adultery while Pharisees crowd around them in the temple. Jacopo Palma the Younger made the etching, which fills the upper half of a sheet that carries two images. It comes from De Excellentia et Nobilitate Delineationis Libri Duo, a drawing book that Giacomo Franco published in 1611. The woman kneels at the left, held by a man beside her. Christ has a halo.

meta: Hercules Segers's small etching of the Rijnsburg abbey ruins, printed in black on prepared linen.
about: Hercules Segers printed this small view of the ruined Rijnsburg abbey on linen instead of paper. The cloth was prepared with a bluish-grey ground, and the ink is black. Transparent grey-blue and yellow paint was added over it. The museum's record notes spots where the etching ground broke down while the plate was bitten. A gothic gable with pointed windows stands behind broken walls and one tall pillar. Pieter Cornelis, Baron van Leyden, owned the sheet before it went to the Koninklijke Bibliotheek. The museum got it in 1816.

meta: Geometria, a seated woman with a compass and a table of diagrams, engraved by Jacob Gole in 1670 for a series on the liberal arts.
about: Geometry appears as a seated woman with a compass in her hand and a table before her holding a sheet of geometric figures. Jacob Gole engraved the print in 1670. It belongs to a series of seven on the seven liberal arts. She wears elaborate period dress and curled hair, and her gaze turns toward the viewer. Look at the diagrams on the sheet.

meta: A double portrait of the brothers Konrad and Franz Eberhard, a painter and a sculptor, printed after a painting by Johann Anton Ramboux.
about: Two men in near profile fill this print, one in a dark cap and cloak at the front and the other in a buttoned coat and cravat behind him. They are the brothers Konrad and Franz Eberhard, a painter and a sculptor. Johann Anton Ramboux made the print after his own painting of them, dated 1822. The painting is in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum in Cologne. Inscriptions in the corners and the lower margin name the sitters.

meta: The death of Dido around a raised bier, a pen and ink drawing by Pietro Testa that the Rijksmuseum bought in a group of fifty in 1946.
about: Mourners gather around a raised bier with a reclining figure at its centre in Pietro Testa's pen drawing of the death of Dido. Draped women stand and kneel in the foreground. The sheet has a long record behind it. In 1946 the museum bought it from the dealer J.L. Reichlen in Lausanne, together with 49 other drawings, for 500 Swiss francs. It was transferred in 1948.

meta: Christopher Columbus carried into a house and greeted by the people of America, a design by Jan Goeree for a book illustration.
about: Two men in loincloths carry Columbus into a room where half-naked men sit on the floor. Two of them kiss the hand and foot of one of his companions. Through the doorway a village and more people can be seen. Jan Goeree drew this as a design for a book illustration. It belongs to a group made for J.L. Gottfried's book of sea and land voyages, published from 1706 to 1727. The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1941 from the dealer H.J. Holgen for 40 guilders.

meta: Hernán Cortés received by Montezuma, a design by Jan Goeree for a book illustration, bought by the Rijksmuseum in 1941.
about: A crowded plaza surrounds a canopied palanquin under a palm tree, with figures in feathered headdresses gathered around it. Armed men in European dress stand at the left. This is Hernán Cortés being received by Montezuma. Jan Goeree drew it in pen and brown, with grey wash and white body colour, as a design for a book illustration. It was made for J.L. Gottfried's book of sea and land voyages. The museum bought it in 1941 from the dealer H.J. Holgen for 40 guilders together with a second Goeree sheet.

meta: A man with a sword and shield, women and children before a wooden building, a design by Jan Goeree for a book illustration.
about: A man in a loincloth stands at the left with a sword and a shield. At the right two women and a child sit in the foreground, and another child stands beside the man. All of them have stretched earlobes, and the standing child seems to have a small weight hanging from the right ear. A wooden building and a few more figures fill the background. Jan Goeree made the drawing as a design for an illustration in J.L. Gottfried's book of sea and land voyages. The museum bought it in 1966.

meta: Galleys at sea in a drawing by Jan Goeree, perhaps a design for a book illustration or print, bought by the Rijksmuseum in 1963.
about: Several galleys ride the sea, with rows of oarsmen under a raised deck crowded with soldiers holding spears and shields. A canopied stern and a distant fleet fill the background. The Rijksmuseum calls the scene a fantasy or a historicising view of an event from Roman or Greek antiquity, such as an imperial visit. Jan Goeree may have made it as a design for a book illustration or a print. The museum bought the sheet in 1963 from a man named Brouwer in Apeldoorn for 25 guilders.
